module.purpose: Provides a React hook that forwards wheel events from focused editor overlays to the canvas unless the pointer is over a genuine scrollable element.
module.summary: This module integrates overlay DOM elements with the editor canvas wheel interaction model. It detects actual scrolling ancestors using overflow dimensions and computed overflow styles, prevents default handling when appropriate, redispatches a marked wheel event to the canvas, and marks the original event to prevent duplicate forwarding. React effects track ref replacement and remove listeners during teardown.
module.businessContext: Supports editor navigation across panels, minimaps, comments, and other overlays while preserving intentional scrolling. Failure can make canvas zoom/navigation unavailable or cause nested panels to scroll incorrectly.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The hook is invoked without a ref.
moduleContractTests.then: throws Error('usePassThroughWheelEvents must be passed a ref')

moduleContractTests.scenario: A wheel event occurs while the editor is not focused.
moduleContractTests.then: the event is neither prevented nor redispatched to .tl-canvas
moduleContractTests.rationale: Wheel pass-through is enabled only for a focused editor.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A focused-editor wheel event originates within an overflowing element with scrollable computed overflow.
moduleContractTests.then: the event is not prevented and no wheel event is dispatched to .tl-canvas
moduleContractTests.rationale: Real scroll containers retain ownership of wheel input.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A focused-editor wheel event occurs outside every scrollable element and a canvas exists.
moduleContractTests.then: preventDefault(e) is called and a new wheel event marked isSpecialRedispatchedEvent is dispatched on .tl-canvas
moduleContractTests.rationale: Non-scrollable wheel input must be transferred to the canvas exactly once.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A wheel event already marked as specially redispatched is received.
moduleContractTests.then: the event is ignored without preventing it or dispatching another wheel event
moduleContractTests.rationale: The marker prevents recursive or duplicate redispatch.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The ref points to a different element after a render.
moduleContractTests.then: the wheel listener is removed from the previously attached element and added to ref.current with passive false
moduleContractTests.rationale: RefObject changes do not notify React, so listener ownership must follow the current element.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The component using the hook unmounts.
moduleContractTests.when: the cleanup returned by the second useEffect runs
moduleContractTests.then: the wheel listener is removed and attached.current is set to null
moduleContractTests.rationale: Unmount cleanup prevents stale listeners and retained DOM references.

detail.name: isScrollable
preconditions: elm is an HTMLElement with readable scrollHeight, clientHeight, scrollWidth, and clientWidth properties.
postconditions: Returns true only when the element overflows vertically or horizontally and the corresponding computed overflow policy is scrollable.
Returns false when the element does not overflow in either direction.
invariants: Computed styles are requested only when vertical or horizontal overflow exists.
Vertical overflow is evaluated against overflowY and horizontal overflow against overflowX.
edgeCases: An element with no vertical or horizontal overflow returns false without resolving computed styles.
An element overflowing only vertically returns the result of evaluating its overflowY policy.
An element overflowing only horizontally returns the result of evaluating its overflowX policy.
An element overflowing in both directions returns true if either corresponding overflow policy is scrollable.
detail.summary: Determines whether an element has overflowing content in a direction whose computed overflow policy permits scrolling. It avoids resolving computed styles when the element does not overflow in either direction.

invariants: The root is included in the scrollability check.
The function does not mutate the target, root, or DOM state.
edgeCases: When target is null or is not a Node, scrollability is checked only on root.
When target is an Element, traversal begins at that element.
When target is a non-Element Node, traversal begins at its parentElement.
When the root is reached without finding a scrollable element, returns false.
When the ancestor chain ends before reaching root without finding a scrollable element, returns false.
detail.summary: Determines whether the wheeled target or one of its ancestors through the specified root is a scrollable HTML element. Non-Node targets are evaluated against the root itself.

postconditions: A wheel listener is attached to the current referenced element when one exists.
When an eligible wheel event occurs, its default action is prevented and a marked wheel event is dispatched to the editor canvas if the canvas exists.
The attached listener is removed when the referenced element changes or the owning component is torn down.
invariants: Wheel events are forwarded only while the editor instance reports that it is focused.
Already redispatched wheel events are never redispatched again.
Wheel events whose target is within a scrollable element are allowed to scroll normally.
The currently attached element is tracked independently from ref.current.

If the editor is absent or not focused, the wheel event is ignored without being prevented or redispatched.
If the event is marked isSpecialRedispatchedEvent, it is ignored.
If the wheel target is within a scrollable element of the referenced container, the event is ignored.
If ref.current is null, no wheel listener is attached.

When ref.current changes, the listener is removed from the previously attached element and added to the new element.
